python_foundations_beginner.name: f-strings
python_foundations_beginner.after: The spec sits after the colon
moved: `sep` is applied between arguments and `end` after the last one. An empty `sep` glues the values together, so `user8814checkout` cannot be split apart again; the newline `end` is the default and leaves the subtotal on a line of its own. The pipe rarely appears in ids or event names, which is why exports use it as a delimiter, though a field that contains one still breaks the split.

python_foundations_beginner.name: Precedence and augmented assignment
moved: The broken line divides only `discount_cents` by 100, because `/` binds tighter than `-`, so the output is 14992.0, a cent total with 5 dollars subtracted from it. Wrapping the subtraction in parentheses makes the whole cent amount divide, and the result is 144.97 dollars. A bug like this prints a plausible number every time it runs, which is why a total that is 100 times too large is worth a parenthesis check before anything else.

python_data_structures_beginner.heading: ### Capstones
moved: The third capstone builds 2 collections from the same list of readings, and each answers a different count. `len` of a set counts distinct values, while `len` of a tuple counts every reading, repeats included. `max` returns the same highest value from either one, because dropping repeats never removes the largest value, only extra copies of it.

The last capstone depends on what square brackets mean on a dict built from pairs. `dict()` makes the first item of each pair a key, so a dict built from (name, quantity) pairs is read with a name. A position number between the brackets asks for a key that is that number, and when no such key exists the lookup stops with a `KeyError` naming the missing key.
